changelog:
AEGIS (v8.0.4) - The fleet reports itself: the lighthouse landing page is now live data.
- [ADD] A station now reports the software version it is running when it registers with its lighthouse. The lighthouse is the only place that sees every station, so it is the only place where "what is actually deployed out there" can be known - and it is known without any station contacting a third party.
- [ADD] The lighthouse landing page no longer states a hand-typed release number. It shows the newest version any registered station has reported, taken from the directory response itself: same origin, no third-party request, and nothing to forget to update when a release goes out. It describes the fleet as it is rather than as someone last remembered it. Each station card also carries the version that station reported, so a lagging node is visible at a glance.
- [ADD] The lighthouse accepts, sanitises and stores a reported version, and tolerates hubs installed before the field existed: the column is added on demand the first time it is needed, so no hub operator has to re-run a run-once installer. An older station that reports no version is still listed, and never erases a version another registration already recorded.
- [SECURITY] The reported version arrives on a public unauthenticated endpoint, so it is treated as untrusted: length-capped, restricted to characters that can appear in a version string, and rejected outright otherwise. A leading "v" is normalised away so the directory does not render "vv8.0.4".
- [ADD] The lighthouse now has a test suite and CI. tests/version_test.php covers validation, the self-healing migration and the fleet tally, against both the current schema and the schema as it was before this release.
- [NOTE] Two mistakes were made while building this and are now pinned by that test: the migration originally matched only SQLite's "no such column" wording (which is what SELECT says - an INSERT says "table X has no column named Y"), and PDO's SQLite driver raises an unknown column from prepare() rather than execute(), so a try block around execute() alone caught nothing.
- [NOTE] The version is reported when the station registers, which happens when its settings are saved. A station upgraded without touching its settings will show its previous version until the next save.
- [NOTE] Carries forward the v8.0 security overhaul, the v8.0.1 and v8.0.2 fixes, and the v8.0.3 peer resilience work. See RELEASE_NOTES.md.
